\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{தீயணைப்பான்} (tīyaṇaippāṉ)}{தீயணைப்பான் (tīyaṇaippāṉ)}]{\ta{தீயணைப்பான்} (tīyaṇaippāṉ) — a fire extinguisher}

\label{lesson:TA-C552-tiyanaippan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for property, then the Tamil for reality.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{தீயணைப்பான்}}
\textbf{\ta{தீயணைப்பான்}} — \emph{tīyaṇaippāṉ} — \textquotedblleft{}a fire extinguisher\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{சமையலறையில்} \ta{தீப்பிடித்தால்} \ta{அப்பா} \ta{தீயணைப்பானைப்} \ta{பயன்படுத்துவார்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{camaiyalaṟaiyil tīppiṭittāl appā tīyaṇaippāṉaip payaṉpaṭuttuvār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the kitchen catches fire, Father will use the fire extinguisher.
\end{quote}

\ta{தீ} \textquotedblleft{}fire\textquotedblright{} + \ta{அணைப்பான்} \textquotedblleft{}that which puts out\textquotedblright{}, from \ta{அணை} (\emph{aṇai}).

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{தீயணைப்பான்}} (\emph{tīyaṇaippāṉ}) is a modern native compound: \ta{தீ} (\emph{tī}), \textquotedblleft{}fire\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 3266), and \ta{அணைப்பான்} (\emph{aṇaippāṉ}), \textquotedblleft{}that which puts out\textquotedblright{}, from \ta{அணை}, \textquotedblleft{}to quench\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 121).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tīyaṇaippāṉ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tīyaṇaippāṉ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{camaiyalaṟaiyil tīppiṭittāl appā tīyaṇaippāṉaip payaṉpaṭuttuvār.} — If the kitchen catches fire, Father will use the fire extinguisher.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for property, then the Tamil for reality, then say \emph{tīyaṇaippāṉ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{தீயணைப்பான்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A fire extinguisher\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{சிலிண்டர்} (ciliṇṭar)}{சிலிண்டர் (ciliṇṭar)}]{\ta{சிலிண்டர்} (ciliṇṭar) — a gas cylinder}

\label{lesson:TA-C552-cilintar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for reality, then the Tamil for a fire extinguisher.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{சிலிண்டர்}}
\textbf{\ta{சிலிண்டர்}} — \emph{ciliṇṭar} — \textquotedblleft{}a gas cylinder\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{சிலிண்டர்} \ta{கசிந்தால்} \ta{உடனே} \ta{சன்னல்களைத்} \ta{திறக்க} \ta{வேண்டும்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ciliṇṭar kacintāl uṭaṉē caṉṉalkaḷait tiṟakka vēṇṭum.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the cylinder leaks, the windows must be opened at once.
\end{quote}

Written with the final \ta{ர்} of the English word.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{சிலிண்டர்}} (\emph{ciliṇṭar}) is a loan from English \emph{cylinder}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ciliṇṭar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ciliṇṭar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ciliṇṭar kacintāl uṭaṉē caṉṉalkaḷait tiṟakka vēṇṭum.} — If the cylinder leaks, the windows must be opened at once.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for reality, then the Tamil for a fire extinguisher, then say \emph{ciliṇṭar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{சிலிண்டர்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A gas cylinder\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{மிதவை} (mitavai)}{மிதவை (mitavai)}]{\ta{மிதவை} (mitavai) — a buoy; a float}

\label{lesson:TA-C552-mitavai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a fire extinguisher, then the Tamil for a gas cylinder.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{மிதவை}}
\textbf{\ta{மிதவை}} — \emph{mitavai} — \textquotedblleft{}a buoy; a float\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{நீச்சல்} \ta{தெரியாவிட்டால்} \ta{மிதவையைப்} \ta{பிடித்துக்கொள்ள} \ta{வேண்டும்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nīccal teriyāviṭṭāl mitavaiyaip piṭittukkoḷḷa vēṇṭum.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you can't swim, you must hold on to the float.
\end{quote}

From \ta{மித} (\emph{mita}), to float: the thing that floats.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{மிதவை}} (\emph{mitavai}) is built on the native \ta{மித} (\emph{mita}), \textquotedblleft{}to float\textquotedblright{}; the formation with -\ta{வை} is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mitavai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mitavai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nīccal teriyāviṭṭāl mitavaiyaip piṭittukkoḷḷa vēṇṭum.} — If you can't swim, you must hold on to the float.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a fire extinguisher, then the Tamil for a gas cylinder, then say \emph{mitavai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{மிதவை} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A buoy; a float\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{துரிதப்படுத்து} (turitappaṭuttu)}{துரிதப்படுத்து (turitappaṭuttu)}]{\ta{துரிதப்படுத்து} (turitappaṭuttu) — to speed up; to expedite}

\label{lesson:TA-C552-turitappatuttu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a gas cylinder, then the Tamil for a buoy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{துரிதப்படுத்து}}
\textbf{\ta{துரிதப்படுத்து}} — \emph{turitappaṭuttu} — \textquotedblleft{}to speed up; to expedite\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{வேலையைத்} \ta{துரிதப்படுத்தினால்} \ta{வெள்ளிக்கிழமைக்குள்} \ta{முடிக்கலாம்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vēlaiyait turitappaṭuttiṉāl veḷḷikkiḻamaikkuḷ muṭikkalām.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If we speed up the work, we can finish by Friday.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{துரிதப்படுத்தினேன்}, \emph{turitappaṭuttiṉēṉ}.

\ta{துரிதம்} \textquotedblleft{}speed\textquotedblright{} + -\ta{ப்படுத்து} \textquotedblleft{}to make\textquotedblright{}. What is sped up takes -\ta{ஐ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{துரிதப்படுத்து}} (\emph{turitappaṭuttu}) is built on \ta{துரிதம்} (\emph{turitam}), \textquotedblleft{}speed\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{tvarita}, \textquotedblleft{}hasty, quick\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the Tamil ending -\ta{ப்படுத்து}, \textquotedblleft{}to make so\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{turitappaṭuttu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{turitappaṭuttu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vēlaiyait turitappaṭuttiṉāl veḷḷikkiḻamaikkuḷ muṭikkalām.} — If we speed up the work, we can finish by Friday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a gas cylinder, then the Tamil for a buoy, then say \emph{turitappaṭuttu} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{அவகாசம்} (avakācam)}{அவகாசம் (avakācam)}]{\ta{அவகாசம்} (avakācam) — time to act; a grace period}

\label{lesson:TA-C552-avakacam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a buoy, then the Tamil for to speed up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{அவகாசம்}}
\textbf{\ta{அவகாசம்}} — \emph{avakācam} — \textquotedblleft{}time to act; a grace period\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{பணம்} \ta{கட்ட} \ta{இன்னும்} \ta{ஒரு} \ta{வார} \ta{அவகாசம்} \ta{கொடுத்தார்கள்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{paṇam kaṭṭa iṉṉum oru vāra avakācam koṭuttārkaḷ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They gave one more week of time to pay the money.
\end{quote}

One gives or asks for it: \ta{அவகாசம்} \ta{கொடு}, \ta{அவகாசம்} \ta{கேள்}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{அவகாசம்}} (\emph{avakācam}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{avakāśa}, \textquotedblleft{}space, room, opportunity\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 728).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avakācam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avakācam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṇam kaṭṭa iṉṉum oru vāra avakācam koṭuttārkaḷ.} — They gave one more week of time to pay the money.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a buoy, then the Tamil for to speed up, then say \emph{avakācam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
